Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person who likes to argue about anything
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Contentious"** means a person who likes to argue about anything; someone who is prone to causing disputes or arguments. (झगड़ालू)

 
 
• **Example: **John is known to be **contentious**, often challenging others' opinions just for the sake of argument.
 
 
 
• **"Contentious"** refers to someone who is argumentative or likely to cause controversy. (झगड़ालू)
 
 
• **Example: **The** contentious** lawyer was always ready to debate every point in the case.
 
 

Hence, we can infer that the correct one-word substitute for a person who likes to argue about anything is **"Contentious"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Reticent **(मितभाषी): Someone who is not revealing one's thoughts or feelings readily.

 
 
• **Example:** The reticent student rarely participated in class discussions.
 
 
 
• **Coward **(कायर ): A person who lacks the courage to face danger, difficulty, opposition, pain, etc.
 
 
• **Example: **He was labeled a coward for not standing up to the bully.
 
 
 
• **Veracious** (सत्यवादी): A person who is habitually truthful and honest.
 
 
• **Example:** The veracious witness provided an accurate account of the events.
